To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the peritubular vascular system of the developing kidney is derived from the metanephrogenic capillaries and the glomerular capillaries.

the peritubular vasculature of puppies is immature, and that the development of the peritubulavascular system occurs in the following order: (1) endothelial cells, (2) basal laminae, (3) pericytes, and (4) smooth muscle cells.
the developing peritubular vascular system is composed of a network of fenestrated endothelial cells that form capillaries, and that this vascular network is supported by a network of pericytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ultrastructural development of the peritubular vasculature of the canine kidney.
the development of the vascular system in the dog kidney.
the study of the development of the vascular system of the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ultrastructural development of peritubuliary capillaries in the puppy kidney is a continuous, step‐wise progression of cellular events that are similar in many ways to those occurring in the adult kidney.
the peritubular vascular system of the kidney develops from a primitive capillary network that is formed by the proliferation and differentiation of mesenchymal cells.
the developing peritubular vascular system in the kidney is composed of capillaries that are lined by a continuous endothelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

peritubular vessels develop by sprouting and by anastomosing preexisting capillaries, that the endothelial cells of developing peritubular microvessels are not fenestrated, and that the peritubular vascular system is a continuous network.
the peritubular vessels are formed by the fusion of the capillary loops that surround the developing nephron and the glomerulus.
peritubular vessels develop from capillary‐like vessels in the mesenchyme, which become surrounded by tubular epithelium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peritubular vessels in the puppy kidney are composed of endothelial cells, pericytes, and vascular smooth muscle cells.
peritubular vessels in the developing dog kidney are fenestrated and lined by a single layer of endothelial cells that are joined by tight junctions and desmosomes.

the peritubular vascular bed of the kidney develops in the following manner: 1) capillary sprouts arise from existing vessels, 2) the sprouts elongate and anastomose to form a capillary network, 3) fenestrations form in the capillaries, 4) the capillaries acquire a continuous basement membrane, and 5) the capillarity is lined by a continuous endothelium.
